title: On the phase transition for the number of collisions on comb graphs
summary: We consider collisions of simple random walks on comb graphs $\mathrm{Comb}(\mathbb{Z},H)$, which are obtained by attaching vertical segments of the form $[0,H_x] \cap \mathbb{Z}$ to any point $x$ of the integer axis. For $\mathrm{Comb}(\mathbb{Z},H)$ with profile $H_x(x) = |x| \log^γ(|x| \vee 1)$, we show that two independent simple random walks starting from the same site collide infinitely often almost surely if $γ\leq 2$.
